autor: The court of Pierre Cauchon and Jean Le Maistre; the record kept by the notaries Manchon, Boisguillaume and Taquel
quelle: J. Quicherat (ed.), Procès de condamnation et de réhabilitation de Jeanne d'Arc, dite la Pucelle, vol. I (Paris: Renouard, 1841), pp. 442–475. Internet Archive, procsdecondam01joanuoft. Public domain.
hinweis: Six excerpts read against the page images: the French minute where it survives, the abjuration in its French form, and the Latin of the sentences. The execution is not carried here. Cuts are marked [...]. The English is this site's working translation (CC0).

sections.blurb: In the cemetery of Saint-Ouen, before a sermon, a crowd and the executioner's cart: her appeal to the pope refused, the abjuration in French signed with a mark, the sentence to perpetual prison, and the women's clothes put on the same afternoon.

units.titel: In the cemetery of Saint-Ouen: 'to God first, and to the pope'
units.orig: Post prædicationem, dominus prædicator dixit eidem Johannæ: « Veecy Messeigneurs les juges, qui plusieurs fois vous ont sommée et requise que voulsissiez submectre tous vous fais et dis à nostre mère saincte Eglise ; et que, en ses diz et fais, estoient plusieurs choses, lesquels, comme il sembloit aux clercs, n'estoient bonnes à dire ou soustenir. » A quoy elle respond : « Je vous respondray. » Et à la submission de l'Église, dist : « Je leur ay dit en ce point de toutes les œuvres que j'ay faictes, et les diz, soient envoyées à Romme devers nostre saint père le Pape, auquel et à Dieu premier je me rapporte. Et quant aux dis et fais que j'ay fais, je les ay fais de par Dieu. » Item dit que de ses fais et dis elle ne charge quelque personne, ne son roy, ne autre ; et s'il y a quelque faulte, c'est à elle et non à autre. Interroguée se les fais et dis qu'elle a fais, qui sont reprouvez, s'elle les veult révoquer : respond : « Je m'en raporte à Dieu et à nostre saint père le Pape. » Et pour ce que il luy fut dit que il ne suffisoit pas, et que on ne povoit pas pour.... aler quérir nostre saint Père si loing ; aussi que les Ordinaires estoient juges chacun en leur diocèse ; et pour ce estoit besoing qu'elle se rapportast à nostre mère saincte Eglise, et qu'elle tenist ce que les clercs et gens en ce se congnoissans en disoient et avoient déterminé de ses diz et fais ; et de ce fut amonnestée jusques à la tierce monicion. Et après ce, comme la sentence fut encommancée à luire, elle dist qu'elle vouloit tenir tout ce que les juges et l'Eglise vouldroient dire et sentencier, et obéir du tout à l'ordonnance et voulenté d'eulx. [...] Et dist plusieurs fois que, puisque les gens d'église disoient que ses apparicions et révélacions n'estoient point à soustenir ne à croire, elle ne les vouloit soustenir ; mais du tout s'en rapportoit aux juges et à nostre mère saincte Eglise.
units.en: After the sermon, the preacher said to Jeanne: 'Here are my lords the judges, who have many times summoned and required you to submit all your deeds and words to our mother holy Church; and that in your words and deeds there were several things which, as it seemed to the clerks, were not good to say or maintain.' To which she answers: 'I will answer you.' And as to submission to the Church, she said: 'I have told them on this point: let all the works I have done, and the words, be sent to Rome to our holy father the pope, to whom, and to God first, I refer myself. And as for the words and deeds I have done, I did them on God's behalf.' Item, she says that for her deeds and words she charges no one, neither her king nor any other; and if there is any fault, it is hers and no one else's. Asked whether she will revoke those of her deeds and words that are condemned, she answers: 'I refer myself to God and to our holy father the pope.' And because she was told that this was not enough, and that one could not go and fetch our holy father so far; also that the Ordinaries were judges each in his own diocese; and that therefore she must refer herself to our mother holy Church, and hold what the clerks and people learned in these things said and had determined about her words and deeds; and she was admonished on this up to the third admonition. And after this, when the sentence had begun to be read, she said she would hold all that the judges and the Church would say and sentence, and obey wholly their ordinance and will. [...] And she said several times that, since the men of the Church said that her apparitions and revelations were not to be maintained or believed, she would not maintain them; but referred herself wholly to the judges and to our mother holy Church.
units.note: Thursday 24 May 1431, in the cemetery of the abbey of Saint-Ouen at Rouen, on a scaffold before a great crowd and in the presence of Cardinal Beaufort, the great-uncle of Henry VI. The preacher was Guillaume Érard. Her appeal to the pope was refused on the spot; the canonists of Paris had submitted their own verdict to the pope (Art. University [3]). The margin of the Latin record notes that she submitted 'before the end of the sentence, fearing the fire' (Ante finem sententiæ, Johanna timens ignem). The sentence being read was the sentence of condemnation that would be read in full on 30 May. The cut is the clerk's line announcing the abjuration.

units.orig: « Toute personne qui a erré et mespris en la foy chrestienne, et depuis, par la grâce de Dieu, est retournée en lumière de vérité et à l'union de nostre mère saincte Église, se doit moult bien garder que l'ennemi d'enfer ne le reboute et face recheoir en erreur et en damnacion. Pour ceste cause, je Jehanne, communément appellée la Pucelle, misérable pécherresse, après ce que j'ay cogneu les las de erreur ouquel je estoie tenue, et que, par la grâce de Dieu, sui retournée à nostre mère saincte Église, affin que on voye que non pas fainctement, mais de bon cuer et de bonne volonté, sui retournée à icelle, je confesse que j'ay très griefment péchié, en faignant mençongeusement avoir eu révélacions et apparicions de par Dieu, par les anges et saincte Katherine et saincte Marguerite, en séduisant les autres, en créant folement et légièrement, en faisant supersticieuses divinacions, en blaphemant Dieu, ses Sains et ses Sainctes ; en trespassant la loy divine, la saincte Escripture, les droiz canons ; en portant habit dissolu, difforme et deshonneste contre la décence de nature, et cheveux rongnez en ront en guise de homme, contre toute honnesteté du sexe de femme ; en portant aussi armeures par grant présumpcion ; en désirant crueusement effusion de sang humain ; [...] Confesse aussi que j'ay esté scismatique et par pluseurs manières ay erré en la foy. Lesquelz crimes et erreurs, de bon cuer et sans ficcion, je, de la grâce de nostre Seigneur, retournée à voye de vérité, par la saincte doctrine et par le bon conseil de vous et des docteurs et maistres que m'avez envoyez, abjure de ceste regnie, et de tout y renonce et m'en dépars. [...] Aussi je vous jure et prometz [...] que jamais, par quelque enhortement ou autre manière, ne retourneray aux erreurs devant diz, desquelz il a pieu à nostre Seigneur moy délivrer et oster ; mais à tousjours demourray en l'union de nostre mère saincte Eglise, et en l'obéissance de nostre saint père le Pape de Romme. Et cecy je diz, afferme et jure par Dieu le Tout-Puissant, et par ces sains Évangiles. Et en signe de ce, j'ay signé ceste cédule de mon signe. » Ainsi signée : « Jehanne ✠. »
units.en: 'Every person who has erred and done wrong in the Christian faith, and since, by the grace of God, has returned to the light of truth and to the union of our mother holy Church, must take great care that the enemy of hell does not drive him back and make him fall again into error and damnation. For this cause I, Jeanne, commonly called the Maid, a miserable sinner, having recognised the snares of error in which I was held, and having, by the grace of God, returned to our mother holy Church, so that it may be seen that I have returned to her not feignedly but with a good heart and good will, confess that I have sinned most grievously, in pretending falsely to have had revelations and apparitions from God, through the angels and Saint Catherine and Saint Margaret; in seducing others; in believing foolishly and lightly; in making superstitious divinations; in blaspheming God, his saints male and female; in transgressing the divine law, holy Scripture and the canon law; in wearing a dissolute, misshapen and indecent dress against the decency of nature, and hair cropped round like a man's, against all the decency of the female sex; in bearing arms also with great presumption; in cruelly desiring the shedding of human blood; [...] I confess too that I have been schismatic and have erred in the faith in many ways. These crimes and errors, with a good heart and without pretence, I, by the grace of our Lord returned to the way of truth through the holy teaching and good counsel of you and of the doctors and masters you sent me, abjure and renounce and depart from them all. [...] And I swear and promise you [...] that never, by any persuasion or in any other way, will I return to the said errors, from which it has pleased our Lord to deliver me; but will remain always in the union of our mother holy Church and in obedience to our holy father the pope of Rome. And this I say, affirm and swear by God Almighty and by these holy Gospels. And in sign of this I have signed this schedule with my mark.' So signed: 'Jehanne ✠'.
units.note: The text of the 'cedula' as it stands in the record, followed there by a Latin version. The record says she pronounced it herself and signed it with her own hand. Witnesses of the nullity trial said that the schedule read to her at Saint-Ouen was short, 'about the length of a Pater noster', and that what stands in the record is much longer; the difference became one of the questions of 1456. The cuts give the rest of the list of crimes and her submission to the Church's correction.

units.titel: 'The bread of sorrow and the water of affliction'
units.orig: [...] Verum quia sæpius caritative monita et diutius exspectata, tandem, Deo opitulante, ad gremium sanctæ matris Ecclesiæ rediens, prout credimus, corde contrito et fide non ficta tuos errores ore aperto revocasti, [...] ab excommunicationis vinculis quibus tenebaris adstricta, te absolvimus per præsentes ; si tamen ad Ecclesiam vero corde et fide non ficta redieris, injunctaque tibi et injungenda per nos, servaveris. Quoniam vero in Deum et sanctam Ecclesiam, ut præfertur, temere deliquisti, ad peragendum salutarem pœnitentiam, in perpetuum carcerem, cum pane doloris et aqua tristitiæ, ut ibi commissa defleas et deflenda postea non committas, gratia et moderatione nostris salvis, finaliter et definitive condemnamus. » [...] Item, eadem die jovis, post meridiem, nos, frater Johannes Magistri, vicarius antedictus, [...] accessimus ad locum carceris in quo protunc dicta Johanna aderat, [...] exponendo ei quod, casu quo reverteretur ad talia, de cætero amplius Ecclesia ipsam non reciperet, sed ex toto relinqueret. Præterea eidem dictum fuit quod vestes viriles dimitteret et muliebres acciperet, prout eidem per Ecclesiam fuerat ordinatum. Quæ quidem Johanna respondit quod libenter ipsas vestes muliebres acciperet et per cuncta viris ecclesiasticis pareret et obediret. Ipsasque vestes muliebres sibi oblatas, illico depositis vestibus virilibus, induit, atque insuper capillos quos in rotundum tonsos per prius habebat, abradi et deponi voluit et permisit.
units.en: [...] But because, having been many times charitably admonished and long waited for, at last, with God's help, returning to the bosom of holy mother Church, with a contrite heart and unfeigned faith, as we believe, you have openly revoked your errors, [...] we absolve you by these presents from the bonds of excommunication in which you were held; provided that you have returned to the Church with a true heart and unfeigned faith, and keep what we have enjoined and shall enjoin on you. But because you have rashly sinned against God and holy Church, as said above, we finally and definitively condemn you, to do salutary penance, to perpetual prison, with the bread of sorrow and the water of affliction, that there you may weep for what you have done and do no more what must be wept for, saving our grace and moderation. [...] Item, the same Thursday, after noon, we, brother Jean Le Maistre, the said vicar, [...] went to the place of the prison where the said Jeanne then was, [...] explaining to her that if she went back to such things, the Church would not receive her again, but would abandon her entirely. She was told besides to leave off men's clothes and take women's, as the Church had ordered her. And the said Jeanne answered that she would gladly take the women's clothes and obey the churchmen in all things. And she put on the women's clothes offered her, taking off the men's at once, and also wished and allowed the hair, which she had before worn cut round, to be shaved and taken away.
units.note: The 'mitigated' sentence of 24 May, and the visit to her prison the same afternoon. 'The bread of sorrow and the water of affliction' (pane doloris et aqua tristitiæ) is the formula of perpetual imprisonment. The prison she was taken back to was not a church prison but her cell in the castle, under English guard: one of the points the nullity trial would make. The warning of the afternoon is the condition of what follows.

sections.blurb: Found again in men's clothes, she says why: the promises not kept, the irons, the men around her; and that her voices had told her that she had damned herself to save her life, and that what she said she said 'for fear of the fire'.

units.titel: 'Because they did not keep their promise to me'
units.orig: [...] respond qu'elle a nagaires reprins ledit abbit d'omme, et lessié l'abit de femme. Interroguée pourquoy elle l'avoit prins, et qui luy avoit fait prandre : respond qu'elle l'a prins de sa voulenté, sans nulle contraincte, et qu'elle ayme mieulx l'abit d'omme que de femme. Item luy fut dit qu'elle avait promis et juré non reprandre ledit abbit de homme. Respond que oncques n'entendi qu'elle eust fait serement de non le prandre. Interroguée pour quelle cause elle l'avait reprins : respond que, pour ce qu'il luy estoit plus licite de le reprendre et avoir habit d'omme, estant entre les hommes, que de avoir habit de femme. Item, dit qu'elle avoit reprins, pour ce que on ne luy avoit point tenu ce que on luy avoit promis, c'est assavoir qu'elle iroit à la messe et recepvroit son Sauveur, et que on la mectroit hors de fers. Interroguée s'elle avoit abjuré et mesmement de celui habit non reprandre : respond qu'elle ayme mieulx à mourir que de estre ès fers ; mais se on la veult laisser aler à la messe et oster hors des fers, et meictre en prison gracieuse, et qu'elle eust une femme, elle sera bonne et fera ce que l'Église vouldra.
units.en: [...] she answers that she has lately taken the said man's dress again and left the woman's dress. Asked why she had taken it, and who had made her take it: she answers that she took it of her own will, without any compulsion, and that she prefers a man's dress to a woman's. Item, she was told that she had promised and sworn not to take the said man's dress again. She answers that she never understood that she had sworn not to take it. Asked for what reason she had taken it again: she answers that it was more lawful and fitting for her to take it again and have a man's dress, being among men, than to have a woman's dress. Item, she says that she took it again because what had been promised her had not been kept, namely that she would go to mass and receive her Saviour, and that she would be taken out of irons. Asked whether she had abjured, and in particular promised not to take that dress again: she answers that she would rather die than be in irons; but if they will let her go to mass and take her out of irons, and put her in a gracious prison, and she might have a woman with her, she will be good and do what the Church wishes.
units.note: Monday 28 May 1431, in her cell in the castle, before the judges and eight others. 'Among men': her guards were English soldiers. The French minute adds one thing the Latin record leaves out: 'and that she might have a woman with her' (et qu'elle eust une femme). How she came to be in men's clothes again, whether her women's clothes were taken from her, was disputed by the witnesses of 1456.

units.orig: Interroguée se, depuis jeudi, elle a point ouy ses voix : respond que ouil. Interroguée qu'elles luy ont dit : respond qu'elles luy ont dit que Dieu luy a mandé par sainctes Katherine et Marguerite, la grande pitié de la trayson que elle consenty en faisant l'abjuracion et révocacion, pour sauver sa vie ; et que elle se dampnoit pour sauver sa vie. Item, dit que, au devant de jeudi, que ses voix lui avoient dit ce que elle feroit, et qu'elle fist ce jour. Dit oultre que ses voix luy distrent en l'eschafault que elle respondit ad ce prescheur hardiement, et lequel prescheur elle appelloit faulx prescheur, et qu'il avoit dit plusieurs choses qu'elle n'avoit pas faictes. Item, dist que, se elle diroit que Dieu ne l'avoit envoyée, elle se dampneroit ; que vray est que Dieu l'a envoyée. Item, dist que ses voix luy ont dit depuis, que avoit fait grande mauvestié de ce qu'elle avoit fait, de confesser qu'elle n'eust bien fait. Item, dit que de paour du feu, elle a dit ce qu'elle a dit. [...] Item, dit qu'elle n'a point dit ou entendu révoquer ses apparicions, c'est assavoir que ce fussent sainctes Marguerite et Katherine ; et tout ce qu'elle a fait, c'est de paour du feu, et n'a rien révoqué que ce ne soit contre la vérité. Item, dit qu'elle ayme mieulx faire sa pénitance à une fois, c'est assavoir à mourir, que endurer plus longuement paine en chartre. Item, dit qu'elle ne fist oncques chose contre Dieu ou la foy, quelque chose que on luy ait fait révoquer ; et que ce qui estoit en la cédule de l'abjuracion, elle ne l'entendoit point.
units.en: Asked whether since Thursday she has heard her voices: she answers yes. Asked what they told her: she answers that they told her that God had sent her word, through Saints Catherine and Margaret, of the great pity of the treason to which she had consented in making the abjuration and revocation to save her life; and that she was damning herself to save her life. Item, she says that before Thursday her voices had told her what she would do, and what she did that day. She says besides that her voices told her on the scaffold to answer that preacher boldly; and she called that preacher a false preacher, and said he had said several things of her that she had not done. Item, she said that if she were to say that God had not sent her, she would damn herself; for the truth is that God sent her. Item, she said that her voices have told her since that she did a great wrong in what she did, in confessing that she had not done well. Item, she says that what she said, she said for fear of the fire. [...] Item, she says that she did not say or mean to revoke her apparitions, that is, that they were Saints Margaret and Catherine; and all that she did was for fear of the fire, and she revoked nothing that was not against the truth. Item, she says she would rather do her penance once and for all, that is, by dying, than endure longer pain in prison. Item, she says she never did anything against God or the faith, whatever they made her revoke; and that what was in the schedule of the abjuration, she did not understand.
units.note: The same session, 28 May. In the margin of the Latin record a hand wrote 'Responsio mortifera', the deadly answer. The cut asks her about the crown of the sign, and her answer that she had told the truth about it in the trial. With these words the condition the canonists had set, that she affirm her errors obstinately and in her right mind, was declared fulfilled (Art. University [3]). The next day the judges consulted the assessors, who voted that she was relapsed.

sections.blurb: The sentence as relapsed and heretic, read in the Old Market of Rouen: cast out 'as a rotten limb' and left to the secular power.

units.orig: « In nomine Domini, amen. Quotiens hæresis pestiferum virus uni membrorum Ecclesiæ pertinaciter inhæret, atque ipsum in membrum Satanæ transfigurat, diligenti studio curandum est ne, per reliquas partes mystici corporis Christi, serpere possit hujus perniciosæ labis nefanda contagio. [...] Cum itaque nos, Petrus, miseratione divina Belvacensis episcopus, et frater Johannes Magistri, [...] judices competentes in hac parte, te, Johannam, vulgariter dictam la Pucelle, in varios errores variaque crimina schismatis, idolatriæ, invocationis dæmonum, et alia permulta incidisse, justo judicio declaraverimus; et nihilominus, quoniam Ecclesia non claudit gremium redeunti, nos, existimantes te pura mente et fide non ficta ab hujuscemodi erroribus et criminibus recessisse, dum certa die illis renunciasti et publice jurasti, vovisti atque promisisti nunquam in ipsos errores aut quamcumque hæresim [...] te fore reversuram; [...] deinceps vero, post hujuscemodi tuorum errorum abjurationem, irruente et seducente cor tuum auctore schismatis et hæresis, te in eosdem errores et in præfata crimina, ex tuis confessionibus spontaneis et assertionibus iterum (proh dolor!) incidisse, velut canis ad vomitum reverti solet, sufficienter et manifeste constat; [...] hinc est quod te in sententias excommunicationis, quas primitus incurreras, et in errores pristinos reincidisse declarantes, te relapsam et hæreticam decernimus, et per hanc sententiam nostram, quam pro tribunali sedentes, in his scriptis proferimus et pronuntiamus, te tanquam membrum putridum, ne cætera membra pariter inficias, ab ipsius Ecclesiæ unitate rejiciendam et ejus corpore abscidendam, necnon potestati sæculari relinquendam, decernimus, prout rejicimus, abscidimus et relinquimus; rogantes eamdem potestatem sæcularem quatenus, citra mortem et membrorum mutilationem, circa te suum judicium moderetur; et si in te vera pœnitentiæ signa apparuerint, tibi ministretur pœnitentiæ sacramentum. »
units.en: 'In the name of the Lord, amen. Whenever the poisonous venom of heresy clings obstinately to one of the members of the Church and transforms it into a member of Satan, great care must be taken that the abominable contagion of this pernicious stain does not creep through the other parts of the mystical body of Christ. [...] Since, then, we, Pierre, by divine mercy bishop of Beauvais, and brother Jean Le Maistre, [...] competent judges in this matter, declared by a just judgment that you, Jeanne, commonly called the Maid, had fallen into various errors and various crimes of schism, idolatry, invocation of demons and very many others; and nevertheless, because the Church does not close her bosom to one who returns, we, believing that you had withdrawn from these errors and crimes with a pure mind and unfeigned faith, when on a certain day you renounced them and publicly swore, vowed and promised never to return to those errors or to any heresy [...]; but since then, after this abjuration of your errors, the author of schism and heresy rushing in and seducing your heart, it is sufficiently and manifestly established by your own spontaneous confessions and assertions that you have fallen again (alas!) into the same errors and crimes, as a dog returns to its vomit; [...] therefore, declaring that you have fallen back into the sentences of excommunication you first incurred and into your former errors, we decree that you are relapsed and a heretic; and by this our sentence, which, sitting in judgment, we pronounce in this writing, we decree that you, as a rotten limb, lest you infect the other members likewise, are to be cast out from the unity of the Church, cut off from her body, and left to the secular power, as we do cast you out, cut you off and leave you; praying the said secular power to moderate its judgment upon you short of death and the mutilation of limbs; and if true signs of penitence appear in you, that the sacrament of penance be administered to you.'
units.note: Wednesday 30 May 1431, in the Old Market of Rouen, after a sermon by Nicolas Midi. The plea to the secular power to spare her life and limbs was the canonical formula with which the Church handed over a condemned heretic; it was not meant to be granted, and it was not. The cuts are the citations of the Church Fathers and the second clause about her false contrition. The record does not describe what followed. The burning is told by the witnesses of the nullity trial, in a module planned for later.
